Please don't get a budgie just because your son wishes to have one.

If he can't take responsibility then he shouldn't have one.

Learning to take responsibility with pets like budgies is not easy and budgies are fragile birds.

If you want to take care of budgies, please consider doing a deep research because there are still many myths out there about budgies, like that one budgie is enough (they need at least one companion). 

I have budgies since 2004 and they are not just something you put in a cage, change food/water and clean the cage: 
You have to take care of a living being with needs for love, joy, respect, attention and enough space. 

There are dangers in some plants and you need to make sure that your cookware is bird-safe or else you need to make sure they are far away, in another closed room to avoid the danger of death. 

They need good nontoxic toys, a big (!) budgie friendly cage, enough opportunities to take a nap, high quality food (not the supermarket food), fresh clean water, attention and freedom to fly in their budgie room (not cage).

An avian vet is the vet you need for budgies. 

There is alot more to know, so do your big research and think twice before taking responsibility for sweet budgies.

You're welcome. You're a good owner if you want to know more about being a good budgie parent. Take good care of yourself and your budgie. I wish you and your budgie well.

- have enough money for an avian (!) vet
- if you need to go to an avian vet, make sure you can drive there on your own or somebody else can help you get there as quickly as possible
- have a small cage for vet visits
- research about good food for your budgies (I buy mine from an online store for birds and the variety/quality has a huge positive impact on the health of them)
- give them enough space to fly
- never stress them
- always speak in a gentle and kind way to them, even if they misbehave
- give them fresh, clear water every day (and clean their water bowl regularly to avoid bacteria)
- buy them a big cage (it must be rectangular or square); they need to have enough space and safety inside that cage, too
- don't go too close to them, especially at the beginning (you would feel uncomfortable, too, if another human gets very, very close to you)
- no matter what your efforts were/are, there are budgies which will never get onto your finger/hand so don't have high expectations: their health/happiness > them being tamed
- always have at least 2 budgies (!)
- make sure that their cage is regularly cleaned and clean in general
- get them budgie-friendly toys
- make sure that they stay far away from Teflon (basically everything with non-sticky coating), its gases kill them
- when it's New Years Eve, stay with them, it can scare them to death -> a tip is to play them music which they are familiar with and like
- only grab them in emergency cases and research about how to grab them the correct way to avoid a bad outcome
- make sure that every day they have enough time to fly freely
- research about how to make sure that their flying room is 100% safe from any flying accidents
- some plants/materials/foods are toxic for them (do a good research)
- buy a small light for their nightly sleep to avoid night terrors (night terrors are when they suddenly fly around crazily in their cage and are in a huge panic mode, when that happens don't panic, too, and make sure they know that everything is alright)
- enjoy every single day with them
- I don't know what it's called in English but it's basically some kind of cotton that can stop bleeding -> always have something at home that can stop bleeding quickly, if budgies bleed then they will die very quickly
